claim: Pancreatic acinar cells can be directly converted to insulin+ β-cells in adult mouse pancreas by combined actions of three transcription factors, Ngn3, Pdx1, and Mafa (referred to as M3 factors).
source: We reported previously that pancreatic acinar cells can be directly converted to insulin+ β-cells in adult mouse pancreas by combined actions of three transcription factors, Ngn3, Pdx1, and Mafa (referred to as M3 factors) (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhou et al., 2008) and is a statement of previously published findings.

claim: Ngn3 alone induces formation of somatostatin+ cells in approximately 40% of infected cells.
source: Surprisingly, Ngn3 alone induced formation of somatostatin+ (Sst) cells in approximately 40% of infected cells (Figure 1B–D)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D and quantified in the text.

claim: Mafa or Pdx1 alone did not induce any hormone positive cells.
source: whereas Mafa or Pdx1 alone did not induce any hormone positive cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Co-infection of Ngn3 and Mafa induces formation of both glucagon+ and somatostatin+ cells, which are distinct from each other.
source: In addition, co-infection of Ngn3- and Mafa-induced formation of both glucagon+ (Gcg) and somatostatin+ cells, which are distinct from each other (Figures 1E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claim: The other two-factor combinations, Ngn3 with Pdx1 and Pdx1 with Mafa, did not yield hormone positive cells.
source: The other two-factor combinations, Ngn3 with Pdx1 and Pdx1 with Mafa, did not yield hormone positive cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Somatostatin and glucagon are the principle hormones of endocrine δ- and α-cells.
source: Somatostatin and glucagon are the principle hormones of endocrine δ- and α-cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about pancreatic endocrine cell types.

claim: Different combinations of three reprogramming factors can convert pancreatic acinar cells in vivo to the three major islet endocrine cell types: δ-, α- and β-cells.
source: These data suggest that different combinations of three reprogramming factors could convert pancreatic acinar cells in vivo to the three major islet endocrine cell types: δ-, α- and β-cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing different factor combinations produce different cell types.

claim: The expression of reprogramming factors in δ- and α-cell induction is transient.
source: The expression of reprogramming factors in δ- and α-cell induction is transient (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), similar to β-cell induction using the same experimental approach (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and comparison to prior work.

claim: The majority of induced δ-like cells co-express Sst and Cckbr 30 days after induction (87 ±7% by immunohistochemistry).
source: Our analysis revealed that the majority of induced δ-like cells co-express Sst and Cckbr 30 days after induction (87 ±7% by immunohistochemistry, Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2A with quantification.

claim: Cholecystokinin receptor B (Cckbr) is a δ-cell-specific gene.
source: Among the few δ-cell-specific genes identified are somatostatin and cholecystokinin receptor B (Cckbr) (Morisset et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Morisset et al., 2000).

claim: The Sst+ cells express the endocrine factors Pax6 and synaptophysin.
source: The Sst+ cells also express the endocrine factors Pax6 and synaptophysin (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: The Sst+ induced δ-cells were present in adult pancreas 2 months after induction.
source: The Sst+ induced δ-cells were present in adult pancreas 2 months after induction (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The secretory granules of induced δ-cells are spherical or ellipsoidal with matrix filling the entire granule space.
source: Electron microscopy analysis revealed that the secretory granules of induced δ-cells are spherical or ellipsoidal with matrix filling the entire granule space (Figure 2E,E′).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2E and E'.

claim: The morphology of induced δ-cell granules is typical of endogenous δ-cells and distinct from that of α-or β-granules.
source: This morphology is typical of endogenous δ-cells (Figure 2D,D′) and distinct from that of α-or β-granules (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of electron microscopy images in Figures 2D, D' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The induced δ-cells were embedded among acinar cells.
source: In addition, we observed that the induced δ-cells were embedded among acinar cells (Figure 2E, arrow points to dense assembly of endoplasmic reticulum in a neighboring acinar cell), consistent with their origins from acinar cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2E and inference about their origin.

claim: Endogenous δ-cells reside exclusively within islets.
source: In contrast, endogenous δ-cells reside exclusively within islets (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2D and represents established knowledge about pancreatic anatomy.

claim: Gene profiling yielded 1283 genes enriched in the induced δ-cells (30 days after induction) relative to acinar cells.
source: Gene profiling with illumina arrays yielded 1283 genes enriched in the induced δ-cells (30 days after induction) relative to acinar cells (GEO: GSE52522).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression profiling data deposited in GEO database.

claim: 632 of the induced genes (49%) overlapped with the islet-enriched gene set.
source: 632 of the induced genes (49%) overlapped with the islet-enriched gene set that we previously reported (Figure 2F) (Zhou et al., 2008) (GEO: GSE12025).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of gene expression datasets shown in Figure 2F and cited prior work.

claim: δ-cells represent a minor fraction of total mouse islet cells (5.5% as determined by FACS).
source: Given that δ-cells represent a minor fraction of total mouse islet cells (5.5% as determined by FACS, see Figure 2—figure supplement 4)
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Among the top 30 most highly induced genes in the δ-like cells, many show low expression in whole islet samples.
source: Indeed, among the top 30 most highly induced genes in the δ-like cells, many show low expression in whole islet samples (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Hhex is up-regulated in induced δ-cells.
source: We detected up-regulation of Hhex (Figure 2G), a gene recently implicated in δ-cell biology (72nd ADA abstract, Klaus Kaestner lab).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2G and citation to conference abstract.

claim: Glucagon, insulin, and the β-cell marker Nkx6.1 are abundantly expressed in islets but absent from induced δ-cells.
source: In contrast, glucagon, insulin, and the β-cell marker Nkx6.1 are abundantly expressed in islets but absent from induced δ-cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Insulin2 gene expression is regulated by DNA sequences located within approximately 400 bp upstream of the transcription start site (TSS).
source: Studies have shown that insulin2 gene expression is regulated by DNA sequences located within approximately 400 bp upstream of the transcription start site (TSS) (Hay and Docherty, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Hay and Docherty, 2006).

claim: Approximately 200 bp of the Amylase 2 promoter is sufficient to direct acinar-specific expression.
source: Similarly, approximately 200 bp of the Amylase 2 promoter is sufficient to direct acinar-specific expression (Minami et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Minami et al., 2005).

claim: None of the CpG sites assayed in the somatostatin promoters was methylated in all samples tested.
source: None of the CpG sites assayed in the somatostatin promoters was methylated in all samples tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), indicating that this promoter is not subject to regulation by DNA methylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5 and inference about regulatory mechanism.

claim: Amylase2 was largely unmethylated in acinar cells.
source: Amylase2, a gene exclusively expressed in pancreatic acinar cells, was largely unmethylated in acinar cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The induced δ-cells showed strong methylation in the Amylase2 promoter similar to islet δ-cells.
source: In contrast, the induced δ-cells showed strong methylation in this promoter similar to islet δ-cells (Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: The Insulin2 promoter was fully methylated in acinar cells but partially demethylated in both endogenous and induced δ-cells.
source: The Insulin2 promoter was fully methylated in acinar cells but partially demethylated in both endogenous and induced δ-cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: For both amylase and Insulin promoters, the methylation differences of acinar/islet δ-cell and acinar/induced δ-cell are statistically highly significant (p<0.001).
source: For both amylase and Insulin promoters, the methylation differences of acinar/islet δ-cell and acinar/induced δ-cell are statistically highly significant (p<0.001)
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of DNA methylation data.

claim: There is no significant difference in DNA methylation between islet δ-cells and induced δ-cells (p=0.23 and 0.30 for amylase and insulin promoter respectively).
source: whereas there is no significant difference between islet δ-cells and induced δ-cells (p=0.23 and 0.30 for amylase and insulin promoter respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of DNA methylation data.

claim: Substantial DNA methylation changes occurred during acinar to δ-cell conversion in the promoters studied.
source: These studies suggest that substantial DNA methylation changes occurred during acinar to δ-cell conversion in the promoters we studied.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the DNA methylation data presented.

claim: Not all cell fate conversion events are associated with DNA methylation changes.
source: It is notable that not all cell fate conversion events are associated with DNA methylation changes.
evidence: This is a general statement based on knowledge from the field.

claim: No significant DNA methylation was observed in the conversion of pre-B cells to macrophages.
source: For example, no significant DNA methylation was observed in the conversion of pre-B cells to macrophages (Rodriguez-Ubreva et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Rodriguez-Ubreva et al., 2012).

claim: The induced δ-cells responded to Arginine and released somatostatin, in a manner similar to isolated islets which contain endogenous δ-cells.
source: The induced δ-cells responded to Arginine and released somatostatin, in a manner similar to isolated islets which contain endogenous δ-cells (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by radioimmunoassay data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Control acinar cells did not respond to Arginine stimulation.
source: In contrast, control acinar cells did not respond to Arginine stimulation (Figure 2I), consistent with the fact that they do not express endocrine hormones.
evidence: This claim is supported by radioimmunoassay data shown in Figure 2I and inference based on known biology.

claim: Induced δ-cells possess cellular machineries necessary for hormone production, storage, and release.
source: These data suggest that induced δ-cells possess cellular machineries necessary for hormone production, storage, and release.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the hormone secretion assay data.

claim: δ-like cells induced by Ngn3 expression in adult pancreas possess key features of endogenous δ-cells.
source: The data described above collectively indicate that δ-like cells induced by Ngn3 expression in adult pancreas possess key features of endogenous δ-cells.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from multiple lines of experimental evidence presented.

claim: Co-infection of adult mouse pancreas with two different adenoviruses carrying Ngn3 and Mafa induced formation of glucagon+ cells.
source: Co-infection of adult mouse pancreas with two different adenoviruses carrying Ngn3- and Mafa-induced formation of glucagon+ cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Co-infection with Ngn3 and Mafa also induced somatostatin+ cells, which are distinct from the glucagon+ cells.
source: This co-infection also induced somatostatin+ cells, which are distinct from the glucagon+ cells (Figure 3A′).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A'.

claim: A 1:1 ratio of Ngn3/Mafa viruses yielded the most number of Gcg+ cells (9 ± 5%).
source: We tested different ratios of Ngn3/Mafa viruses and observed that a 1:1 ratio yielded the most number of Gcg+ cells (Figures 1F and 9 ± 5% at 1:1 ratio, and data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and quantification.

claim: Polycistronic co-expression of Ngn3 and Mafa from a single construct yielded substantially reduced number of glucagon+ cells (less than 1%).
source: In contrast to co-infection by two separate viruses, polycistronic co-expression of Ngn3 and Mafa from a single construct yielded substantially reduced number of glucagon+ cells (less than 1%, data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data (not shown in figures).

claim: Arx is the most important gene that controls endogenous α-cell development and identity.
source: The most important gene that controls endogenous α-cell development and identity is the transcription factor Arx.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about α-cell biology.

claim: Genetic deletion of Arx during embryonic development results in the absence of α-cells.
source: Genetic deletion of Arx during embryonic development results in the absence of α-cells, whereas ectopic expression of Arx in β-cells causes their phenotypic drift towards α-cells (Collombat et al., 2003; Dhawan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Collombat et al., 2003; Dhawan et al., 2011).

claim: Ectopic expression of Arx in β-cells causes their phenotypic drift towards α-cells.
source: Genetic deletion of Arx during embryonic development results in the absence of α-cells, whereas ectopic expression of Arx in β-cells causes their phenotypic drift towards α-cells (Collombat et al., 2003; Dhawan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Collombat et al., 2003; Dhawan et al., 2011).

claim: Strong Arx expression was observed in all induced Gcg+ cells.
source: We observed strong Arx expression in all induced Gcg+ cells, although some Gcg− cells also expressed Arx (Figures 3B,B′).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 3B and B'.

claim: All Gcg+ cells expressed the endocrine genes Pax6 and synaptophysin.
source: In addition, all Gcg+ cells expressed the endocrine genes Pax6 (Figure 3C,C′) and synaptophysin (Figure 3D,D′).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 3C, C', D, and D'.

claim: The induced α-cells are readily observable 2 month after induction.
source: The induced α-cells are readily observable 2 month after induction (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Induced α-cells share a similar ultrastructure as the endogenous α-cells.
source: Electron microscopy analysis of the induced α-cells indicates that they share a similar ultrastructure as the endogenous α-cells (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figures 3E and F.

claim: The secretory granules of induced α-cells have a narrow halo between the core and membrane that is typical of α-granules and distinct from δ- and β-granules.
source: The secretory granules have a narrow halo between the core and membrane (Figure 3E′,F′) that is typical of α-granules and distinct from δ- and β-granules (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figures 3E', F' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The induced α-like cells were intermingled among acinar cells.
source: The induced α-like cells were intermingled among acinar cells (Figure 3F, arrow points to zymogene granules of a neighboring acinar cells)
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Endogenous α-cells were found exclusively within islets.
source: whereas endogenous α-cells were found exclusively within islets (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and represents established knowledge.

claim: The acinar fraction that contains induced α-cells responded to the secretagogue Arginine and released glucagon.
source: In an in vitro hormone secretion assay, the acinar fraction that contains induced α-cells isolated from the adult pancreas 30 days after induction responded to the secretagogue Arginine and released glucagon (Figure 3H), indicating their ability to produce and secrete hormone.
evidence: This claim is supported by radioimmunoassay data shown in Figure 3H and inference about cellular function.

claim: DNA methylation analysis showed a general similarity of induced α-cells with endogenous α-cells at the Glucagon, Amylase2a, and Insulin2 promoters.
source: DNA methylation analysis at the Glucagon, Amylase2a, and Insulin2 promoters showed a general similarity of induced α-cells with endogenous α-cells (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Statistical analysis showed no significant difference between endogenous and induced α-cells at glucagon and insulin promoters (p=0.26, 0.50, respectively).
source: Statistical analysis showed no significant difference between endogenous and induced cells at glucagon and insulin promoters (p=0.26, 0.50, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of DNA methylation data.

claim: A difference in DNA methylation was detected at the amylase promoter between endogenous and induced α-cells (p=0.02).
source: However, a difference was detected at the amylase promoter (p=0.02).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of DNA methylation data.

claim: Amylase protein expression was absent in the majority of Gcg+ cells (over 95%).
source: Amylase protein expression was absent in the majority of Gcg+ cells (over 95%).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data.

claim: A small fraction (<5% of all Gcg+ cells) were Amylase+, indicating incomplete reprogramming in a small subset of glucagon+ cells.
source: However, a small fraction (<5% of all Gcg+ cells) were Amylase+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 4), indicating incomplete reprogramming in a small subset of glucagon+ cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4 and inference about reprogramming completeness.

claim: Induced α-cells possess key features of endogenous α-cells.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that induced α-cells possess key features of endogenous α-cells.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from multiple lines of experimental evidence presented.

claim: The acinar cell is the cell-of-origin for most of the induced β-cells in M3 factor-mediated reprogramming of adult pancreas.
source: We previously reported that the acinar cell is the cell-of-origin for most of the induced β-cells in M3 factor-mediated reprogramming of adult pancreas (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhou et al., 2008).

claim: Adenovirus preferentially infects acinar cells but not the other pancreatic cell types.
source: This is in part due to preferential infection of adenovirus for acinar cells but not the other pancreatic cell types (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhou et al., 2008).

claim: Tamoxifen induction of Ptf1aCreER::RosaYFP animals resulted in the labeling of 20–30% of mature acinar cells.
source: Tamoxifen induction resulted in the labeling of 20–30% of mature acinar cells (Figure 4A′,B′), consistent with published report of this line (Pan et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figures 4A' and B' and citation to prior work (Pan et al., 2013).

claim: Acinar cells can give rise to both δ-like and α-like cells after adenoviral delivery of Ngn3 or Ngn3+Mafa.
source: After adenoviral delivery of Ngn3 or Ngn3+Mafa, which targets acinar cells, we confirmed that acinar cells can give rise to both δ-like and α-like cells (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figures 4A and B.

claim: The induced endocrine cells are smaller than acinar cells.
source: The induced endocrine cells are also smaller than acinar cells (Figure 4A,B, arrows), consistent with previous report (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figures 4A and B and citation to prior work (Zhou et al., 2008).

claim: The conversion of acinar cells to induced δ- and α-cells occurred largely in the absence of cell proliferation.
source: Continuous BrdU labeling showed that the conversion of acinar cells to induced δ- and α-cells occurred largely in the absence of cell proliferation (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU labeling data shown in Figures 4C and D.

claim: Only about 1% of the induced δ- and α-cells incorporated BrdU in a 10-day reprogramming period.
source: Only about 1% of the induced δ- and α-cells incorporated BrdU in a 10-day reprogramming period (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU labeling data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Induced δ- and α-cells derive from adult acinar cells.
source: These studies confirmed that induced δ- and α-cells derive from adult acinar cells and that the acinar conversion occurred largely in the absence of cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from lineage tracing and BrdU labeling data.

claim: Ptf1a, Nr5a2, and Mist1 are key acinar cell-fate regulators.
source: Ptf1a, Nr5a2, and Mist1 are key acinar cell-fate regulators.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about acinar cell biology.

claim: Ptf1a, Nr5a2, and Mist1 are expressed in adult acinar cells.
source: They are expressed in adult acinar; their genetic deletion results in abnormalities of acinar development and function (Pin et al., 2001; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Lin et al., 2004; Beres et al., 2006; Holmstrom et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Pin et al., 2001; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Lin et al., 2004; Beres et al., 2006; Holmstrom et al., 2011).

claim: Genetic deletion of Ptf1a, Nr5a2, and Mist1 results in abnormalities of acinar development and function.
source: They are expressed in adult acinar; their genetic deletion results in abnormalities of acinar development and function (Pin et al., 2001; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Lin et al., 2004; Beres et al., 2006; Holmstrom et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Pin et al., 2001; Kawaguchi et al., 2002; Lin et al., 2004; Beres et al., 2006; Holmstrom et al., 2011).

claim: Ngn3 and Mafa, but not Pdx1, strongly suppressed Ptf1a, Mist1, and Nr5a2 expression 4 days after gene delivery in pancreas.
source: We observed that Ngn3 and Mafa, but not Pdx1, strongly suppressed Ptf1a, Mist1, and Nr5a2 expression 4 days after gene delivery in pancreas (Figure 5A,B,E,F,I,J,M).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 5A, B, E, F, I, J, and M.

claim: Pax6 and Islet1 are endocrine genes expressed in all islet endocrine cells.
source: Pax6 and Islet1 are endocrine genes expressed in all islet endocrine cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about pancreatic endocrine cells.

claim: Genetic studies have established the important role of Pax6 and Islet1 in the development of all islet endocrine subtypes.
source: Genetic studies have established their important role in the development of all islet endocrine subtypes (Ahlgren et al., 1997; Sander et al., 1997; Ashery-Padan et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Ahlgren et al., 1997; Sander et al., 1997; Ashery-Padan et al., 2004).

claim: Ngn3, but not Mafa or Pdx1, activated the expression of Pax6 and Islet1 at day 4 after pancreas infection.
source: Ngn3, but not Mafa or Pdx1, activated the expression of these pan-endocrine genes at day 4 after pancreas infection (Figure 5C,D,G,H,K,L,M).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 5C, D, G, H, K, L, and M.

claim: Among the three reprogramming factors, Ngn3 alone possesses the ability to initiate two key events in endocrine reprogramming: acinar suppression and pan-endocrine activation.
source: The data discussed above together indicate that among the three reprogramming factors, Ngn3 alone possesses the ability to initiate two key events in endocrine reprogramming, namely, acinar suppression and pan-endocrine activation, thereby establishing a generic endocrine state in acinar cells.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from the experimental data showing Ngn3's effects on acinar and endocrine genes.

claim: Persistent expression of Nr5a2 strongly blocked induction of Pax6 and Sst compared with Ngn3 alone controls.
source: 10 days after the infection, analyses revealed that persistent expression of Nr5a2 strongly blocked induction of Pax6 and Sst (Figure 6B,E,G), compared with Ngn3 alone controls (Figure 6A,D,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 6A, B, D, E, and G.

claim: Ptf1a similarly suppressed Pax6 and Sst induction.
source: Another acinar factor Ptf1a similarly suppressed Pax6 and Sst induction (Figure 6C,F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 6C, F, and G.

claim: Key acinar factors are potent molecular barriers; their down-regulation is a prerequisite for endocrine reprogramming.
source: These results demonstrate that key acinar factors are potent molecular barriers; their down-regulation is a prerequisite for endocrine reprogramming.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing that persistent acinar factor expression blocks reprogramming.

claim: In Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion, strong suppression of the acinar factor Mist1 was observed at day 2 after Ngn3 delivery.
source: In Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion, we observed strong suppression of the acinar factor Mist1 at day 2 after Ngn3 delivery (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The pan-endocrine gene Pax6 was robustly activated at day 2 after Ngn3 delivery in acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: The pan-endocrine gene Pax6 was also robustly activated at day 2 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Expression of δ-specific genes somatostatin and CCKbr was not detected until day 4 in acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: In contrast, expression of δ-specific genes somatostatin and CCKbr was not detected until day 4 (Figure 7G,H) and became strongly expressed at day 10 (Figure 7K,L).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 7G, H, K, and L.

claim: A similar temporal sequence of acinar suppression (Mist1) and pan-endocrine activation (Pax6) followed by β-specific gene activation (Nkx6.1 and insulin) was observed in acinar to β-cell conversion.
source: A similar temporal sequence of acinar suppression (Mist1) and pan-endocrine activation (Pax6) followed by β-specific gene activation (Nkx6.1 and insulin) was also observed in acinar to β-cell conversion (Figure 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 8.

claim: A generic endocrine state was established in acinar cells at the onset of reprogramming, temporally preceding endocrine subtype specification.
source: These data collectively suggest that a generic endocrine state was established in acinar cells at the onset of reprogramming, temporally preceding endocrine subtype specification.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the temporal analysis data showing pan-endocrine genes are activated before subtype-specific genes.

claim: Polycistronic co-expression of Mafa with Ngn3 reduced the efficiency of somatostatin induction from 40 ± 3% in control Ngn3 animals to 24 ± 7% in Ngn3.Mafa animals.
source: Polycistronic co-expression of Mafa with Ngn3 reduced the efficiency of somatostatin induction from 40 ± 3% in control Ngn3 animals (Figure 9A) to 24 ± 7% in Ngn3.Mafa animals (Figure 9B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 9A, B, and D.

claim: Polycistronic co-expression of Pdx1 with Ngn3 led to near complete suppression of somatostatin+ cells (2 ± 1%).
source: Polycistronic co-expression of Pdx1 with Ngn3 led to near complete suppression of somatostatin+ cells (2 ± 1%, Figure 9C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figures 9C and D.

claim: Cherry+somatostatin− cells were synaptophysin+ when Pdx1 and Ngn3 were co-expressed.
source: Immunostaining with pan-endocrine factor synaptophysin revealed that Cherry+somatostatin− cells were synaptophysin+ (Figure 9C, inset), suggesting that Ngn3 converted acinar cells to an endocrine state, but that δ-subtype specification was blocked.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 9C inset and inference about the cellular state.

claim: Pdx1 and Mafa can suppress δ-subtype specification.
source: These data indicate that Pdx1 and Mafa can suppress δ-subtype specification, which is likely part of the mechanism to ensure formation of distinct α- and β-subtypes upon coexpression of multiple reprogramming factors.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing Pdx1 and Mafa suppress somatostatin induction.

claim: Pancreatic acinar cells can be directly converted to endocrine δ- and α-like cells by in vivo expression of Ngn3 or Ngn3+Mafa respectively.
source: Our studies indicate that pancreatic acinar cells can be directly converted to endocrine δ- and α-like cells by in vivo expression of Ngn3 or Ngn3+Mafa respectively.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Three major islet endocrine subtypes can be derived by acinar reprogramming with defined factors.
source: Together with our previous report of β-cell reprogramming with Ngn3+Mafa+Pdx1, these studies provide a set of reprogramming models where combinatorial actions of three factors lead to conversion of acinar cells to the three major islet endocrine subtypes in vivo (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript and shown in Figure 10A.

claim: Acinar to endocrine reprogramming includes two main processes: establishment of a generic endocrine state and endocrine subtype specification.
source: Our studies indicate that acinar to endocrine reprogramming includes two main processes: establishment of a generic endocrine state and endocrine subtype specification (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from the experimental data and shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Ngn3 plays a central role in promoting the endocrine state at the onset of reprogramming by suppressing acinar fate regulators and activating pan-endocrine genes.
source: Ngn3 plays a central role in promoting the endocrine state at the onset of reprogramming by suppressing acinar fate regulators and activating pan-endocrine genes (Figure 10B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data showing Ngn3's effects and shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Continued expression of key acinar factors will block endocrine conversion.
source: This early step is critical as continued expression of key acinar factors will block endocrine conversion.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing persistent acinar factor expression blocks reprogramming.

claim: Mafa suppresses acinar regulators but does not activate pan-endocrine genes.
source: Compared with Ngn3, Mafa suppresses acinar regulators but does not activate pan-endocrine genes, whereas Pdx1 lacks the ability to initiate either of these two events.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data showing differential effects of the three factors.

claim: Pdx1 lacks the ability to suppress acinar regulators or activate pan-endocrine genes.
source: Compared with Ngn3, Mafa suppresses acinar regulators but does not activate pan-endocrine genes, whereas Pdx1 lacks the ability to initiate either of these two events.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data showing differential effects of the three factors.

claim: The main function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to collaborate with Ngn3 to activate subtype-specific genes such as Arx in α-induction and Nkx6.1 in β-induction.
source: It is likely that the main function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to collaborate with Ngn3 to activate subtype-specific genes such as Arx in α-induction (this study) and Nkx6.1 in β-induction (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citation to prior work (Zhou et al., 2008).

claim: Another important function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to suppress δ-specification, thus ensuring formation of singular α- and β-subtypes, and preventing hybrid cells.
source: Another important function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to suppress δ-specification, thus ensuring formation of singular α- and β-subtypes, and preventing hybrid cells (Figure 10B, lower panel).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing Mafa and Pdx1 suppress somatostatin induction and shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Each of the three factors possesses both activator and suppressor functions.
source: Our data together suggest that each of the three factors possesses both activator and suppressor functions (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from the experimental data and shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Ngn3 can suppress exocrine fate and promote endocrine fate during both embryogenesis in progenitor cells and during adulthood in differentiated acinar cells.
source: During pancreatic development, numerous studies have highlighted the importance of Ngn3 in controlling endocrine fate specification (Jensen, 2004). A recent study showed that ectopic expression of Ngn3 in embryonic pancreas suppressed exocrine fate specification (Qu et al., 2013). Thus, Ngn3 can suppress exocrine fate and promote endocrine fate during both embryogenesis in progenitor cells and during adulthood in differentiated acinar cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the current study's data and citations to prior work (Jensen, 2004; Qu et al., 2013).

claim: The function of Pdx1 has been demonstrated to be critical in early pancreatic fate determination, as well as a later role in beta cell biology.
source: The function of Pdx1 has also been extensively studied and demonstrated to be critical in early pancreatic fate determination, as well as a later role in beta cell biology (Murtaugh, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Murtaugh, 2007).

claim: Mafa is expressed in pancreatic β-cells during development and plays a role in controlling β-cell gene transcription.
source: Mafa is expressed in pancreatic β-cells during development and plays a role in controlling β-cell gene transcription (Hang and Stein, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Hang and Stein, 2011).

claim: Mafb is expressed during pancreas development in a subset of endocrine progenitor cells.
source: Its close homologue Mafb is expressed during pancreas development in a subset of endocrine progenitor cells (Nishimura et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Nishimura et al., 2006).

claim: Mafb deletion leads to decreased α- and β-cell numbers, suggesting a role for Maf factor in α-cell formation.
source: Mafb deletion leads to decreased α- and β-cell numbers, suggesting a role for Maf factor in α-cell formation (Artner et al., 2007; Nishimura et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Artner et al., 2007; Nishimura et al., 2008).

claim: There are clear similarities in the function of Ngn3, Mafa, and Pdx1 in normal endocrine development and endocrine reprogramming from acinar cells.
source: Taken together, there are clear similarities in the function of Ngn3, Mafa, and Pdx1 in normal endocrine development and endocrine reprogramming from acinar cells.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on inference from comparison of developmental and reprogramming data.

claim: The epigenetic landscape of pancreatic progenitors and adult acinar cells in which these factors operate is presumably very different.
source: Nevertheless, the epigenetic landscape of pancreatic progenitors and adult acinar cells in which these factors operate is presumably very different.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on general knowledge about epigenetic differences between progenitor and differentiated cells.

claim: The 'generic endocrine state' established by Ngn3 in acinar cells is not equivalent to an endocrine progenitor in pancreas development.
source: Further, the 'generic endocrine state' established by Ngn3 in acinar cells is not equivalent to an endocrine progenitor in pancreas development.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observation that progenitor markers are not expressed during reprogramming.

claim: Expression of pancreatic progenitor genes such as Sox9 and Hnf6 was not detected during the reprogramming process.
source: For example, expression of pancreatic progenitor genes such as Sox9 and Hnf6 was not detected during the reprogramming process (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data (not shown in figures).

claim: No genetic factors have been discovered that specify δ-cell fate in pancreas development.
source: Among the pancreatic endocrine subtypes, relatively little is known about the δ-cells. No genetic factors have been discovered that specify δ-cell fate in pancreas development.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Conversion of acinar cells to α-cells requires both Ngn3 and Mafa.
source: Conversion of acinar cells to α-cells requires both Ngn3 and Mafa.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The optimal method to induce Gcg+ α-like cells is by co-expression of Ngn3 and Mafa from two separate viruses at a 1:1 ratio.
source: The optimal method to induce Gcg+ α-like cells is by co-expression of Ngn3 and Mafa from two separate viruses at a 1:1 ratio.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data comparing different delivery methods.

claim: Varying the ratio of the two viruses or polycistronic co-expression of both factors led to reduced α-cell formation.
source: Varying the ratio of the two viruses or polycistronic co-expression of both factors led to reduced α-cell formation.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data comparing different delivery methods.

claim: Polycistronic co-expression of OSKM factors led to substantially reduced efficiency of iPS formation compared with random infection by OSKM factors.
source: These results are reminiscent of induced pluripotent reprogramming from fibroblasts where polycistronic co-expression of OSKM factors led to substantially reduced efficiency of iPS formation compared with random infection by OSKM factors (Carey et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Carey et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009).

claim: The difference in iPS formation efficiency has been suggested to result from a need for appropriate reprogramming factor stoichiometry.
source: This difference has been suggested to result from a need for appropriate reprogramming factor stoichiometry (Carey et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Carey et al., 2011).

claim: The induction of α-like cells may require optimized Ngn3/Mafa stoichiometry along with other conditions such as specific expression level and dynamics of the factors.
source: We speculate that the induction of α-like cells may similarly require optimized Ngn3/Mafa stoichiometry along with other conditions such as specific expression level and dynamics of the factors, which can be met at the more 'flexible' co-injection system with each cell expressing variable levels of Ngn3/Mafa, compared with the more 'fixed' polycistronic expression system.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the experimental observations and comparison to iPS reprogramming.

claim: A suitable strategy to produce specific subtypes of cells by lineage conversion is to combine factors that confer broad competence with factors that confer subtype specificity.
source: Our studies suggest that a suitable strategy to produce specific subtypes of cells by lineage conversion is to combine factors that confer broad competence with factors that confer subtype specificity.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: Removal of a chromatin factor and employment of neuron selector genes allows conversion of germ cells to different neuronal subtypes in C. elegans.
source: An elegant example was demonstrated in C. elegans, where removal of a chromatin factor and employment of neuron selector genes allows conversion of germ cells to different neuronal subtypes (Tursun et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Tursun et al., 2011).

claim: The pancreatic islets contain three major hormone-secreting endocrine subtypes: insulin+ β-cells, glucagon+ α-cells, and somatostatin+ δ-cells.
source: The pancreatic islets contain three major hormone-secreting endocrine subtypes: insulin+ β-cells, glucagon+ α-cells, and somatostatin+ δ-cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about pancreatic anatomy.

claim: β-cells secret insulin and play a key role in blood glucose regulation.
source: β-cells secret insulin and play a key role in blood glucose regulation, whereas α- and δ-cells secrete glucagon and somatostatin to support β-cell function (Edlund, 2001; Jensen, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Edlund, 2001; Jensen, 2004) and represents established knowledge.

claim: α- and δ-cells secrete glucagon and somatostatin to support β-cell function.
source: β-cells secret insulin and play a key role in blood glucose regulation, whereas α- and δ-cells secrete glucagon and somatostatin to support β-cell function (Edlund, 2001; Jensen, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Edlund, 2001; Jensen, 2004) and represents established knowledge.

claim: Adenoviruses co-expressing reprogramming factor and mCherry were used to directly induce conversion of acinar cells in adult pancreas.
source: Adenoviruses co-expressing reprogramming factor (R.F.) and mCherry (cherry) were used to directly induce conversion of acinar cells in adult pancreas.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: Phenotypes were analyzed 10 days after induction.
source: Phenotypes were analyzed 10 days after induction.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: Co-expression of Ngn3, Mafa, Pdx1, and mCherry from a single polycistronic construct led to exclusive formation of insulin+ cells in 47 ± 8% of the mCherry+ cells.
source: Co-expression of Ngn3, Mafa, Pdx1, and mCherry from a single polycistronic construct led to exclusive formation of insulin+ cells in 47 ± 8% of the mCherry+ cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the manuscript.
